name: AI-First Process Orchestration — Complete Process & E2E Flow Redesign

relationships.description: D-004 was human-first (catalog + run button). D-005 replaces it with AI-first event-driven orchestration
Module sidebar now needs process orchestration layer underneath
AIS/GPS events from D-003 tracking become triggers for E2E flows
Run Now button replaced by event-driven auto-triggering
Monitor page redesigned for E2E flow tracking, not just process instances

problem_statement.summary: The ERP was built human-first: humans navigate modules, click buttons, enter data. AI agents are helpers called on demand. 227 processes and 20 E2E flows exist as documentation — nothing actually executes. This is a traditional ERP with AI sprinkled on top, not an AI-first ERP.
specific_failures: 81 of 227 processes (35.7%) are ORPHANED — not part of any E2E flow
72 processes (31.7%) are only PARTIALLY covered — the E2E flow mentions the module but not the specific process
All 20 E2E flows have only ~8 steps each — real shipping operations need 15-30 steps per flow
E2E flows reference MODULES, not specific PRC-xxx process IDs — no actual linkage
No transaction-to-process binding — a booking exists in a DB table but nothing knows what E2E flow it should follow
No event-driven triggers — everything waits for a human to click 'Run'
24 entire business areas are MISSING from the process catalog (feeder ops, alliance/VSA, trade finance, tax/VAT, document release, roll-over management, cargo routing, etc.)
Feeder vessel operations — critical for Qatar/UAE/KSA/India market — have near-zero coverage despite feeders being the primary connectivity for Hamad Port, smaller Indian ports, and KSA ports

content.decision: Complete redesign of the process and E2E flow layer into an AI-first, event-driven orchestration system where: (1) AI agents are primary operators executing processes 24/7, (2) humans are decision-makers brought in only at explicit gates, (3) every transaction automatically triggers the correct E2E flow(s), (4) every step is tracked with full auditability, (5) every one of ~280 processes belongs to at least one E2E flow — zero orphans.
ai_first_principles: AI is the OPERATOR, humans are SUPERVISORS — AI executes 90% of steps, humans handle decisions, exceptions, and approvals
EVENT-DRIVEN, not click-driven — when a booking is confirmed, a vessel arrives, a payment is received, the system acts immediately without human initiation
TRANSACTIONS ARE FLOWS — a booking IS a Booking-to-Cash flow instance. A container IS an Import/Export flow instance. Creating the transaction creates the flow.
CASCADING FLOWS — one E2E flow creates sub-entities (booking creates containers, containers create BLs, BLs create invoices) and each sub-entity can trigger its own E2E flow
HUMAN GATES are explicit — every point where a human must decide is defined with: who, what info they see, SLA for decision, escalation if SLA breached
FULL TRACEABILITY — at any moment, for any transaction, you can see exactly where it stands, what happened, what's next, and who's responsible
PROACTIVE, not reactive — AI predicts problems (feeder delay, customs hold risk, SLA breach) and acts before humans even notice

target_state.transaction_binding: every transaction type mapped to E2E flow(s)
target_state.event_triggers: ~60 event types triggering flow creation or step advancement

missing_business_areas.description: 24 business areas identified as completely or significantly missing from the current 227 processes

areas.why_critical: Before anything else, the system must determine HOW cargo gets from A to B: direct, hub-spoke, multi-transshipment, which vessels, which feeders, transit time options

Hamad Port (Qatar), smaller Indian ports, KSA ports are served primarily by feeders. Feeder ops have different lifecycle: shorter voyages, connection timing is critical, feeder BL management, hub coordination
Most shipping lines operate through alliances or VSAs. Slot purchase/sale, revenue sharing, schedule coordination, equipment interchange with partners
Door-to-door vs CY-CY terms define who manages inland transport. Trucking, rail, drayage, last-mile delivery coordination
Many Middle East and India transactions involve L/Cs. Bank guarantees payment upon compliant document presentation
Qatar (no VAT yet), UAE (5% VAT), KSA (15% ZATCA), India (18% GST + customs duty). Multi-country tax calculation, filing, withholding tax
Invoicing in customer currency, settlement in different currency, FX gain/loss calculation, hedging contracts
Physical BL originals must be released. Telex release, surrender at origin/destination, switch BL at intermediate port, express release, seaway bill — daily documentation function
Cargo that can't be loaded on planned vessel rolls to next sailing. Happens DAILY. Major customer pain point — affects trust and SLA
Each port/vessel has multiple cut-offs: documentation, VGM, cargo receiving, DG — different deadlines that must be enforced
When customs holds cargo for examination — duty payment, physical inspection, documentation review. Must be managed as part of import flow
Own or contracted depots: gate hours, inspection capacity, M&R vendors, storage charges, empty stock levels
Contract volume commitments, rebate calculation based on actual vs committed, quarterly/annual settlement

areas.area: Liner Agency (acting AS agent for another line)
areas.why_critical: Many Gulf shipping companies act as liner agents for other lines. Different business model — earn commission, handle port ops, documentation for another line
Non-Vessel Operating Common Carrier: house BL on top of master BL, LCL consolidation/deconsolidation, CFS management
Vessel waiting at anchorage (common at Indian ports), terminal closures, equipment shortages. Must manage operational disruptions
Beyond claims — policy renewal, premium calculation, coverage assessment, H&M surveys, P&I club calls
ROB tracking, consumption per leg vs plan, bunker adjustment for charter hire, bunker clause settlement
For chartered vessels: off-hire period calculation, speed/consumption warranty claims, weather routing disputes
Long-term fleet decisions: buy/sell/charter-in/charter-out, newbuilding orders, S&P market monitoring
Non-containerized cargo has a completely different lifecycle: heavy lift, project logistics, lashing/securing, marine warranty surveyor
Beyond KYC screening — ongoing monitoring of existing customers, mid-contract sanctions, license management for dual-use goods
Trade credit insurance (Euler Hermes, Coface) to protect against customer default — common in shipping
Grounding, collision, fire, piracy — emergency response protocols, salvage coordination, GA (General Average) declaration

transaction_process_binding.description: Every business transaction type maps to one or more E2E flows that are automatically instantiated when the transaction is created or reaches a trigger state

human_gate_architecture.description: Every point where a human must make a decision is an explicit gate in the E2E flow. The AI prepares all information, presents a recommendation, and waits for the human.

gate_types.description: AI completed work, human approves or rejects
gate_types.ui: Approve/Reject buttons with AI recommendation shown

examples: Roll cargo to next vessel or find alternative
Accept or counter customer rate offer
gate_types.ui: Option cards with AI-calculated pros/cons for each

gate_types.description: Human must provide information the system cannot
gate_types.ui: Structured input form with AI-suggested defaults

gate_types.description: AI encountered something it cannot handle
gate_types.ui: Alert with full context, AI analysis, and recommended actions

sla_enforcement.default_sla: 2 hours for approvals, 4 hours for decisions, 24 hours for input
sla_enforcement.escalation_chain: Direct manager → Department head → Operations director
sla_enforcement.auto_approve_rule: If gate type=approval AND AI confidence>95% AND amount<threshold AND no flags → auto-approve after SLA expiry

implementation_plan.description: Phased delivery — each phase is independently valuable. Replaces D-004's 23-feature plan.

phases.phase: Phase 1: Process & Flow Data Complete Rewrite (2-3 sessions)
phases.description: Rewrite operational-processes.ts (227→290 processes) and e2e-process-flows.ts (20→35 flows with 15-30 steps each). Every process mapped to at least one flow. New E2EProcessFlow type with PRC refs, executor types, gate definitions.
deliverables: F-016: New process data — 63 new processes (PRC-228 to PRC-316)
F-017: New E2E flow data — 35 flows, 15-30 steps each, PRC-xxx refs, human gates
F-018: Updated types — E2EFlowStep with processRef, executorType, gateDefinition, triggerCondition

phases.description: DB migration for new tables. Event bus that listens for transaction events and auto-creates E2E flow instances. Step executor that drives AI agents and pauses at human gates.
deliverables: F-019: DB migration — 5 new tables (pe_e2e_flow_instances, pe_e2e_step_instances, pe_human_gates, pe_flow_events, pe_event_triggers)
F-020: Event trigger engine — maps transaction events to E2E flow creation
F-021: Step executor — AI agent execution + human gate creation + step advancement
F-022: Human gate manager — notification, SLA tracking, escalation, auto-approve

phases.phase: Phase 3: Live Monitoring & Human Gate UI (3-4 sessions)
phases.description: Real-time dashboard showing all active E2E flows. Human approval inbox. Flow detail view with step-by-step progress.
deliverables: F-023: E2E Flow Monitor — live dashboard of all active flows with progress
F-024: Flow Detail View — step timeline, current position, history, sub-flows
F-025: Human Gate Inbox — pending decisions with AI recommendations, SLA countdown
F-026: Transaction Process View — for any booking/container/vessel, see all associated flows

phases.phase: Phase 4: AI Agent Execution & Intelligence (2-3 sessions)
phases.description: Wire Claude API for AI agent steps. AI prepares gate information for humans. Proactive risk detection.
deliverables: F-027: AI agent execution service — Claude API integration for process steps
F-028: AI gate preparation — AI analyzes and recommends before human gates
F-029: Proactive alerts — AI detects risks (feeder delay, SLA breach, customs hold) before they happen

phases.description: Process performance analytics, bottleneck detection, AI agent effectiveness tracking.
deliverables: F-030: Process analytics dashboard — completion rates, SLA compliance, bottlenecks
F-031: AI performance tracking — approval rates, human override rates, cost per process

acceptance_criteria: 290 processes defined — zero orphans, every process belongs to at least one E2E flow
35 E2E flows with 15-30 steps each — every step references a PRC-xxx process
Every E2E flow step defines executor type (ai_agent/human/system) and trigger condition
Human gates have gate type, assigned role, SLA, escalation path, and AI recommendation
Transaction-flow binding: creating a booking automatically creates an E2E-01 flow instance
Event triggers: vessel arrival automatically creates E2E-12 port call flow instances
Conditional flow creation: DG cargo booking automatically adds E2E-06 DG flow
Cascading flows: E2E-01 creates child E2E-04 instances per container
Real-time monitoring: at any point, see where every transaction stands in its flow
Human gate inbox: pending decisions with AI recommendation, SLA countdown, escalation
Feeder operations fully covered: E2E-21 and E2E-22 with 11 new processes
All 24 missing business areas addressed with new processes and E2E flows
AI agents execute 70%+ of steps autonomously — humans handle ~30% (gates only)
Full audit trail: every step completion, gate decision, AI output logged immutably
edge_cases: Booking has both DG and reefer cargo — multiple conditional flows triggered simultaneously
Feeder delay causes missed mainline connection — E2E-22 must handle exception routing
Customer credit limit breached mid-flow — E2E-01 must pause at credit gate
AI agent fails (timeout, error) — step retries with backoff, then escalates to human
Human gate SLA expires with no response — auto-approve if low risk, else escalate
Same container in multiple flows (E2E-04 export at origin, E2E-03 import at destination) — flows must not conflict
Cancellation mid-flow — E2E flow must handle graceful termination, notify downstream steps
Roll-over scenario — E2E-01 must branch: cancel current vessel load step, create new E2E-04 on next vessel
Multi-transshipment (cargo goes through 2+ hubs) — nested E2E-07 instances per hub
Alliance cargo — booking on partner's vessel triggers different flow variant
L/C expiring before cargo arrival — E2E-26 must alert before expiry
error_handling: Event trigger fails to create flow — log to pe_flow_events with error, retry 3x with exponential backoff
AI agent step timeout (30s) — mark step failed, create human gate for manual completion
DB transaction failure during step advancement — rollback, retry, log
Human gate notification delivery failure — retry via alternate channel (email → in-app → SMS)
Circular flow dependency detected — prevent, log, alert system admin
Flow instance stuck (no progress for 24h) — auto-alert operations manager
security_considerations: Human gates enforce RBAC — only users with correct role can decide at a gate
AI agent outputs may contain sensitive data — PII masking in logs
Event triggers must validate tenant_id — never cross-tenant flow creation
Auto-approve rules must have financial limits per role (Delegation of Authority matrix)
Audit trail is immutable — no DELETE on pe_flow_events
Gate decisions require authentication — no anonymous approvals
rationale: AI-first is non-negotiable — the competitive advantage IS the AI operating the business 24/7
Event-driven > click-driven — shipping operations don't wait for office hours or human availability
Transaction binding makes processes real — a process without a transaction is just documentation
35 flows covering 290 processes ensures complete operational coverage — nothing falls through cracks
Human gates with AI recommendations make humans more effective — they see the analysis, not raw data
Phased delivery (5 phases, 12-16 sessions) ensures incremental value without context window overflow
Phase 1 (data rewrite) is foundational — everything else depends on having the correct process and flow definitions
